Imbolc Eve Early Lamb Stew

Served at: Imbolc Eve (La Fheile Bride)

Serves 6-8Prep 25 minCook 2 hours 30 min

Imbolc Eve, also known as La Fheile Bride, marks the halfway point between winter and spring, celebrating the first stirrings of new life and the lambing season. This hearty lamb stew honors the promise of spring with tender lamb and root vegetables, providing warmth and sustenance as we anticipate brighter days.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900g) boneless lamb shoulder or leg, cut into 1 1/2-inch (4cm) cubes
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 large yellow onion, chopped
  • 3 carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5cm) pieces
  • 2 celery stalks, chopped
  • 4 medium potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red), peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch (4cm) cubes
  • 1 parsnip, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5cm) pieces (optional, for traditional root flavor)
  • 4 cups (960ml) lamb or beef broth
  • 1 cup (240ml) dry stout or dark ale (optional, or more broth)
  • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 3 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1/4 cup (30g) all-purpose flour (optional, for thickening)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Method

  1. Pat the lamb cubes dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.
  2. In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per batch. Remove the browned lamb to a plate and set aside.
  3. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. If using, stir in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
  4. Return the lamb to the pot. Pour in the broth and stout (if using), scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add the potatoes, parsnip (if using), rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
  5. Bring the stew to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for at least 1 hour 45 minutes, or until the lamb is very tender.
  6. Remove the rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  7. Ladle the hot stew into bowls and garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, brown the lamb well to develop a deep crust.
  • If you prefer a thicker stew, you can mash some of the cooked potatoes against the side of the pot.
  • This stew tastes even better the next day, allowing the flavors to meld further. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
